hints: Focus on what actually carries the current, mobile ions or electrons, and ask what must be free to move in each test.
Y conducts well as a pure liquid, so it must be a molten ionic lattice with free $\text{Na}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ ions.
Z is non-conducting when pure but gives a conducting mixture with water, so think of a covalent chloride that hydrolyses to release $\text{H}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ ions.
walkthrough:
**Recall when a compound conducts**

Conduction needs mobile charged particles. In liquids, this means free mobile ions.

Rule to use:
$$\text{conducts in liquid state = molten ionic compound with mobile ions}$$

**Identify Y from the two good results**

Y conducts both as a pure liquid and when added to water. That is classic for a soluble ionic salt.

For $\text{NaCl}$:
$$\text{NaCl(l)} \rightarrow \text{Na}^+ + \text{Cl}^- \text{(mobile, so conducts)}$$
$$\text{NaCl(aq)} \rightarrow \text{Na}^+(\text{aq}) + \text{Cl}^-(\text{aq}) \text{(mobile, so conducts)}$$
So Y must be $\text{NaCl}$.

**Identify Z from does not conduct, then good**

Z does not conduct as a pure liquid, so it is not ionic. It must be covalent molecular with no mobile ions. When added to water it gives a good conducting mixture, so it must react with water to make ions.

$\text{SiCl}_4$ is covalent tetrahedral and hydrolyses completely:
$$\text{SiCl}_4 + 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{Si(OH)}_4 + 4\text{H}^+ + 4\text{Cl}^-$$
The $\text{H}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ ions formed make the solution conduct well. This matches Z perfectly.

**Check why $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ fits neither row fully**

$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is ionic and would conduct when molten, but it is insoluble in water. Adding it to water gives no mobile ions, so the mixture would not conduct well.

options.A: Y as $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ would conduct when molten, but it is insoluble in water so the water mixture would not conduct well. This contradicts the table where Y conducts well in water.
options.B: Y as $\text{NaCl}$ is correct, but Z as $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ is wrong. Molten $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ contains mobile ions and would conduct, not fail to conduct. Also it does not dissolve to give a conducting aqueous mixture.
options.C: Y as $\text{NaCl}$ is ionic and soluble, so both the melt and the aqueous solution contain mobile $\text{Na}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ and conduct well. Z as $\text{SiCl}_4$ is covalent, so the pure liquid has no ions and does not conduct, but hydrolysis in water produces $\text{H}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ which conduct well.
options.D: This swaps the types. $\text{SiCl}_4$ as Y would not conduct as a pure liquid because it is covalent with no mobile ions. $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ as Z would conduct when molten and would not give a conducting aqueous mixture due to insolubility.
